sentences.text: This species was among eighteen dinosaur taxa described in 2015 through open access or free-to-read journals.
The genus was named and described in 2015 by a research team led by Lü Junchang and Pu Hanyong.
The name Huanansaurus comes from Huanan, the historical name for Southern China.
The specific name ganzhouensis indicates the fossil's origin in the city of Ganzhou.
The main specimen, known as the holotype, comes from the Campanian-Maastrichtian layers of the Nanxiong Formation.
This holotype includes a partially articulated skeleton with a nearly complete skull, lower jaws, neck vertebrae, forelimb bones, and parts of the hindlimb.
The holotype specimen is currently kept at the Henan Geological Museum in Zhengzhou.
In 2026, researchers Hao and Xu assigned a new specimen from the Tangbian Formation to Huanansaurus and suggested that Corythoraptor is a junior synonym.
Another specimen preserved on top of a nest has also been assigned to Huanansaurus and is held at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.
It is placed within the subfamily Oviraptorinae, although the Paleobiology Database lists its parent group as Citipatinae.
Huanansaurus lived approximately 72 million years ago during the late Cretaceous period in what is now China.
